thread:
maria (sec-eng): FYI tenant `acme` onboarding failing. SCIM calls returning 403, SAML auth looks fine, but roles are not provisioned. seeing KMS decrypt errors in the provisioner logs. :frowning:
ken (idp-platform): Can you paste the exact error lines? 403 from SCIM usually means attribute/role mapping or decryption fail on our side. :eyes:
maria (sec-eng): Here's the relevant log snippet from provisioning job (sanitized):
```
2026-01-12T18:03:02Z ERROR provisioner: scim PATCH -> 403 {"detail":"forbidden: unable to decrypt extId: InvalidCiphertextException"}
2026-01-12T18:03:02Z WARN  provisioner: role_map lookup failed for externalId: "acct:acme:roles/ops"
2026-01-12T18:03:02Z DEBUG kms-client: decrypt failed, alias arn:aws:kms:...:alias/rdw-provisioner: InvalidCiphertextException
```
ken (idp-platform): That InvalidCiphertextException usually means either ciphertext was produced with a different key/alias OR the envelope/context didn't match. Did acme rotate their IdP encryption key?
sam (devex): Quick check: can you curl the metadata endpoint and dump the raw XML? sometimes IdP metadata has invisible whitespace in xmlns or weird BOM.
maria (sec-eng): Did that: `curl -s https://idp.acme.example/.well-known/saml-configuration | xmllint --format -` returned odd attrs. Pasting sanitized fragment:
```xml
<EntityDescriptor xmlns = "urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:metadata" entityID="https://idp.acme.example/">
  <IDPSSODescriptor ...>
    <!-- attributes -->
  </IDPSSODescriptor>
</EntityDescriptor>
```
ken (idp-platform): Notice the space around `xmlns =` — our metadata parser is sensitive to attribute tokenization in the library version we're running. It treats that as a different attribute tokenization path which ended up not being normalised before we generated the encrypted extId blob. That could propagate a different canonicalization so KMS decrypt fails when we try to unwrap. :thinking_face:
gita (prod-sec): Also, RBAC mapping: the provisioner expects `urn:acme:roles` in the extId to map to internal roles. If metadata normalization changed entityID or NameID format, the extId could be mismatched. Can we get the raw extId payload (before encryption) for a failed record?
maria (sec-eng): We can reproduce in staging. I dumped the pre-encrypt payload for a failed SCIM user: `{"extId":"acct:acme:roles/ops","attributes":{...}}` and after encryption we store base64 JWE. When decrypt fails, we can fetch the stored ciphertext and re-run decrypt locally.
ida-bot: metadata-update detected for idp.acme.example at 2026-01-12T17:58:00Z (source=onboarder)
ken (idp-platform): Ok, action plan: 1) reproduce decrypt locally with kms-client using stored ciphertext 2) fetch metadata and normalize attribute whitespace then re-run canonicalization 3) if failing, try decrypt with previous KMS alias (maybe they used alternate alias)
sam (devex): Small helpful command for local repro (use staging creds):
```bash
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://ciphertext.bin --key-id alias/rdw-provisioner --encryption-context "extId=acct:acme:roles/ops"
```
If that returns InvalidCiphertext, try `--key-id arn:aws:kms:...:alias/rdw-provisioner-prev`
gita (prod-sec): Also file a quick audit log entry so we can tie failed decrypts to tenant and time. We need that for compliance and postmortem. Maria, add the events to the SSO incident runbook.
maria (sec-eng): Will do. Quick note: prov pipeline currently drops role mapping on any exception — we should change to `probe` mode to keep users created with minimal roles instead of failing entirely. Proposal: fallback to `unmapped` role and create a flagged account for backfill. Thoughts?
ken (idp-platform): Good safety net. But careful: unmapped accounts still need least-privilege. Use `role=read-only` as default. Also emit `scim.provision.fallback` metric.
sam (devex): I'll open a tiny deploy to flip probe-mode for this tenant only and add a metric tag `tenant:acme` — quick rollback if anything odd.
ida-bot: deploy pipeline started: deploy-2026-01-12-18-15-probe-mode-acme (PR #4218)
maria (sec-eng): One more thing: could be KMS context mismatch. We sometimes include `metadata_version` in encryption context. If metadata parser changed, context will differ and KMS will reject. Check provisioner code that builds context.
ken (idp-platform): Confirmed: provisioner v2.4 sets context `{"extId":"...","meta_v":"1"}` while older onboarding used `meta_v=0`. The IdP metadata auto-update bumped canonicalization which made us flip meta_v. We're seeing a mix of ciphertexts produced by both codepaths. Need a decrypt-compatibility path.
gita (prod-sec): For now, do not rotate KMS keys. We'll add a compatibility decryption step in the provisioner: try current context, fallback to previous context, then fallback to returning `403+audit` if both fail. Also log which context matched.
maria (sec-eng): I'm going to escalate to incident response and start a short bridge. tagging @ken and @gita to join.
ken (idp-platform): Joining bridge. I'll grab the ciphertexts for the last 30 fails and run local decrypt attempts.
sam (devex): I'll keep probe-mode PR small and on a short TTL. If rollback needed, I can revert in <10min.
gita (prod-sec): After remediation, we should add a postmortem noting: vulnerable point was strict XML attribute parsing + assumptions in encryption context. Add test that re-parses vendor XMLs with permissive whitespace.
maria (sec-eng): Agree. Created incident ticket INC-2026-0009 and linked PRs + logs. For now we triage under SSO/SCIM: high-severity (affects provisioning, not auth).
ida-bot: incident INC-2026-0009 created and assigned to "sec-eng"
maria (sec-eng): Thanks all. I'll post updates on the bridge. :thumbsup:
